reason: Audited the example. R(z)=(z^2+1)/(z-1)=z+1+2/(z-1): the numerator is 2 at z=1, so the only pole is simple and the coprime polynomials have maximum degree 2. Closed-disc counting gives N(r,infinity;R)=0 for r<=1 (the boundary pole has logarithmic weight log 1=0) and N(r,infinity;R)=log r for r>1. For |z|=r>=4, |R(z)| is between r/2 and 2r, so (1/2)log(1+|R(z)|^2) equals log r+O(1) uniformly on the circle and m(r,infinity;R)=log r+O(1); hence T(r,R)=2log r+O(1). Cross-checks: the degree-two fixed-rational composition law applied to the identity gives 2T(r,z)+O(1)=2log r+O(1), and the rational-degree theorem gives the same. No AC used.
